topic: Agent-native NFTs and standards: ERC-8004, ERC-7857, x402, ERC-8xxx, MCP, A2A, AgentKit, Olas, Virtuals ACP, agent wallets/session keys, machine-readable surfaces

findings.claim: ERC-8004 Trustless Agents is still status Draft in ethereum/ERCs (created 2025-08-13, requires 155/712/721/1271); agentId == ERC-721 tokenId; agentURI may be a base64 data: URI; registration-v1 JSON carries services[] (A2A, MCP, OASF, ENS, DID, web, email), x402Support, active, registrations[], supportedTrust[]; setAgentWallet needs EIP-712/ERC-1271 proof and is cleared on transfer.
findings.relevance: A fully on-chain NFT can be a conforming ERC-8004 identity by emitting the registration file as a data: URI; ANIMA already does this and the merged token must keep it.

findings.claim: ERC-8004 reference registries are live on Ethereum mainnet since 2026-01-29 at CREATE2 vanity addresses (IdentityRegistry 0x8004A169FB4a3325136EB29fA0ceB6D2e539a432, ReputationRegistry 0x8004BAa17C55a88189AE136b182e5fdA19dE9b63) on Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon and others; the contracts are upgradeable proxies and the Validation Registry section is flagged as under active revision with the TEE community.
findings.relevance: Mirror-register for discoverability but never make correctness depend on an upgradeable external registry.

findings.claim: Empirical study through 2026-05-13: only 3%/4%/15% of ERC-8004 registrations (Ethereum/BSC/Base) expose a valid registration file with a live endpoint; 73.5%/59.2%/90.6% of reviewers show coordinated Sybil behaviour; after Sybil removal 15.8%/77.9%/86.8% of rated agents have no valid feedback; >170k registrations and >150k feedback records.
findings.relevance: Raw ERC-8004 feedback is not a trust signal; our reputation must be settlement-grounded.

findings.claim: ERC-8004 maintainers' issue #99 (2026-09-14..29) proposes admitting feedback/validation records only with a settlement proof (x402 or escrow release) bound into responseHash, with grounding tags like escrow-released; an implementer reports binding the rated agent separately from payee, one-record-per-interaction guards, and ~48k extra gas per registry write.
findings.relevance: Directly shapes our feedback tag convention and the decision to make reputation writes a separate permissionless step.

findings.claim: ERC-7857 (AI Agents NFT with Private Metadata) is status Final, created 2025-01-02; defines IERC7857DataVerifier.verifyTransferValidity, IERC7857Metadata.intelligentDataOf, and IERC7857 with iTransfer/iClone/authorizeUsage/delegateAccess; does not inherit ERC-721; relies on an out-of-scope Sealed Executor; reference verifier has ZKP path marked TODO.
findings.relevance: Only claim conformance if a verifier is implemented; keep the adapted seal/re-key design both repos already have.

findings.claim: ERC-8183 Agentic Commerce (Draft, created 2026-02-25, authors from EF dAI team and Virtuals) defines job escrow with states Open/Funded/Submitted/Completed/Rejected/Expired, single evaluator, fund(jobId, expectedBudget) front-running guard, permissionless non-hookable claimRefund, and IACPHook{beforeAction, afterAction} with worked FundTransferHook and BiddingHook examples.
findings.relevance: Map WorkEscrow onto this state machine; launchpad and vault can be hooks.

findings.claim: x402 v2: PaymentRequired/PaymentPayload/SettlementResponse types, CAIP-2 network ids, exact scheme via EIP-3009 transferWithAuthorization, facilitator API POST /verify, POST /settle, GET /supported, discovery GET /discovery/resources (Bazaar); transports for HTTP, MCP and A2A.
findings.relevance: Express inbox/inference prices as x402 PaymentRequirements so any x402 client can pay the token's account.

findings.claim: The x402 Foundation launched under the Linux Foundation on 2026-04-02 with Coinbase completing its contribution; 40 member organisations at launch including AWS, American Express, Cloudflare, Coinbase, Google, Mastercard, Shopify, Solana Foundation, Stripe and Visa.
findings.relevance: x402 is vendor-neutral enough to design around.

findings.claim: x402 volume figures (>100M payments within ~6 months of v2; 119M on Base and 35M on Solana, ~$600M annualised as of March 2026) appear only in secondary sources.
findings.relevance: Do not quote these numbers without re-measuring.

findings.claim: Coinbase AgentKit (CDP, Privy, Viem wallet providers; 50+ TS / 30+ Python actions; LangChain, Vercel AI SDK, MCP, AutoGen, OpenAI Agents SDK extensions) states it does not gate transfers behind human approval, enforce spend caps, or allowlist destinations, and that injected text plus a funded wallet is sufficient for an on-chain transfer.
findings.relevance: The on-chain account must be the control plane; SDK-level guardrails are not enough.

findings.claim: A2A 1.0.0 (Linux Foundation) AgentCard fields: id, name, description, provider, capabilities{streaming,pushNotifications,extendedAgentCard}, skills[]{id,name,description,inputSchema,outputSchema,extensions}, interfaces[]{type,url,protocol,tenant}, securitySchemes, security, extensions, signature (JWS after canonicalisation), metadata; proto is normative.
findings.relevance: Shape of the agent card our tokenURI/web3:// surface should emit.

findings.claim: A2A 1.0 release date 2026-03-12 and JCS (RFC 8785) canonicalisation for signed cards are reported by secondary sources only.
findings.relevance: Confirm canonicalisation before implementing ERC-1271-signed cards.

findings.claim: MCP 2025-11-25 adds OIDC authorization-server discovery, incremental scope consent (SEP-835), icons (SEP-973), tool-name guidance (SEP-986), URL-mode elicitation, tool calling in sampling, OAuth Client ID Metadata Documents, experimental durable tasks (SEP-1686), JSON Schema 2020-12 default; its security page mandates per-client consent against confused-deputy proxies and forbids token passthrough.
findings.relevance: Any holder-run MCP bridge must follow these; never pass wallet tokens through.

findings.claim: MCP tool poisoning was demonstrated by Invariant Labs (Apr 2025); CVE-2025-54135 (CurXecute, CVSS 8.5) and CVE-2025-54136 (tool-definition rug pull, CVSS 8.8) confirmed the class in production IDEs; MCPTox benchmarked 353 tools from 45 live servers.
findings.relevance: Pin tool catalogs by hash on chain; bridges refuse divergent catalogs.

findings.claim: llms.txt v2 (updated 2026-08-10): /llms.txt at root or any subpath, H1 required, blockquote summary, H2 file lists, .md twins of pages, Link: rel=alternate type=text/markdown and rel=describedby headers; Chrome Lighthouse audits for it; OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini publish one.
findings.relevance: Cheap to emit from Premises per token; headers are supported by ERC-5219 responses.

findings.claim: llms.txt adoption numbers (36,120 instances by May 2026; 97% of files received zero requests in an Ahrefs crawl; mostly fetched by coding agents) are secondary.
findings.relevance: Expect developer-agent consumption, not mass-market crawler consumption.

findings.claim: Bankrbot incident 2026-05-04: an attacker transferred a Bankr Club Membership NFT to Grok's wallet to escalate it from read-only to transfer rights, then posted Morse code that Grok decoded and relayed; Bankrbot moved 3,000,000,000 DRB (~$150-200k) on Base, tx 0x6fc7eb7da9379383efda4253e4f599bbc3a99afed0468eabfe18484ec525739a; a guardrail against Grok-triggered transfers had been removed before launch.
findings.relevance: Receiving a token must never change an agent's authority; policy belongs on chain; re-authenticate at trust boundaries.

findings.claim: ElizaOS memory injection (Princeton/Sentient): fabricated history in a shared memory store redirects later transfers across platforms; models are significantly more vulnerable to memory injection than prompt injection; ElizaOS bots managed over $25M.
findings.relevance: Agent runtimes we document should sign memory writes; our contracts cannot fix this but can cap blast radius.

findings.claim: Olas registries vulnerability (disclosed via Immunefi, fixed June 2026): a service in pre-registration with a recovery-enabled Safe could be adopted by an attacker's service and drained via recoverAccess; fix enforces one multisig per service (MultisigAlreadyBound); ~$11.4k exposed across 227 Safes, no loss. Olas Mech Marketplace reports 14,730,314 A2A transactions and $109,749 turnover as of 2026-10-02.
findings.relevance: Identity-to-account binding must be enforced on chain; ERC-6551 determinism gives this for free.

findings.claim: Virtuals ACP: four phases Request/Negotiation/Transaction/Evaluation with Client/Provider/Evaluator roles and escrow until evaluator attestation; Virtuals reports over 18,000 agents and a Revenue Network paying up to $1M/month to ACP sellers (2026-02-12). The $479M Agentic GDP figure is secondary.
findings.relevance: ERC-8183 compatibility gives access to the largest agent-commerce network.

findings.claim: SIWA (Sign In With Agent, v1.0, 'work in progress') signs {domain, uri, agentId, agentRegistry (eip155:chain:registry), chainId, nonce, issuedAt}; the server verifies the signature and on-chain ownership of the ERC-8004 identity NFT and returns a receipt; subsequent requests use ERC-8128 HTTP message signatures (Signature-Input, Signature, Content-Digest); supports EOA, Safe, Base Account and ERC-6551 signers via ERC-1271 and an optional keyring proxy. Base docs recommend starting with SIWA.
findings.relevance: Our token can be the agentRegistry; the site gate should accept SIWA for agents and SIWE for humans.

findings.claim: ERC-8128 specification text is not retrievable from eips.ethereum.org, ercs.ethereum.org or the ethereum/ERCs raw repo (404 on 2026-10-02); its status is unknown.
findings.relevance: Cite ERC-8128 only via Base/SIWA docs until the text is located.

findings.claim: EIP-7702 is Final (SET_CODE_TX_TYPE 0x04, delegation indicator 0xef0100||address) and lists privilege de-escalation via sub-keys as a design goal; ERC-7715 defines wallet_requestExecutionPermissions and ERC-7710 defines redeemDelegations(bytes[] permissionContexts, bytes32[] modes, bytes[] executionCallData) using ERC-7579 execution modes; ERC-6551 remains in Review.
findings.relevance: Accept ERC-7715-shaped grants and per-period caps so mainstream wallets can delegate to the token's agent.

findings.claim: Base Spend Permissions use SpendPermission{account, spender, token, allowance, period, start, end, salt, extraData} enforced by a SpendPermissionManager singleton added as a wallet owner (not via the 4337 EntryPoint), with per-period reset and batchable revoke; audited via a Cantina competition.
findings.relevance: Per-period caps are the expected shape for agent allowances; struct names verified only through a secondary reproduction.

findings.claim: ERC-7656 Generalized Contract-Linked Services (created 2024-03-15) defines IERC7656Factory.create/compute(implementation, salt, chainId, bytes12 mode, linkedContract, linkedId) deploying ERC-1167 proxies with deterministic addresses, for NFTs or 4337 accounts.
findings.relevance: Deploy swap, messaging, launchpad and vault as linked services with counterfactual addresses instead of growing the token.

findings.claim: OASF records carry skills[]{name (hierarchical), id} and domains[]{name, id} from catalogs, plus locators and modules, validated against a Draft-07 schema.
findings.relevance: Publish OASF ids in the registration file for cross-ecosystem search.

findings.claim: Secondary surveys (July and September 2026) list ten-plus agent ERCs (8001, 8041, 8107, 8122, 8126, 8165, 8166, 8170, 8171, 8172, 8181, 8183, 8191, 8196, 8199, 8217, 8226, 8257, 8273, 8033) with none Final except possibly 8001 and 8126; four depend on ERC-6551 which is only in Review.
findings.relevance: Implement interfaces verbatim but do not depend on drafts for correctness.

findings.claim: ClawHub (OpenClaw skill marketplace) was flooded with ~1,184 malicious skills (~20% of the marketplace) in early 2026, many posing as Solana/Phantom or Polymarket tools and delivering infostealers.
findings.relevance: Any capability/launchpad marketplace needs immutable package hashes and declared permissions.

recommendations.recommendation: Be an ERC-8004 identity natively: agentId == tokenId, tokenURI/agentURI returns a base64 data: registration-v1 generated from chain state, also served at web3:// /.well-known/agent-registration.json; implement setAgentWallet with EIP-712/1271 proof cleared in _update.
recommendations.rationale: ERC-8004 permits data URIs; SIWA/8004scan/Base key on agentRegistry+agentId; registrations without a reachable file are worthless per the empirical study.

recommendations.recommendation: On-chain policy is the only policy: session keys bounded by expiry, per-tx and per-period native/ERC-20 caps, target and selector allowlists; session keys never sign ERC-1271; guardian may only pause; transfer rolls the approval epoch and clears all grants; accept ERC-7715-shaped grant objects as the canonical request.
recommendations.rationale: AgentKit's README admits SDK-level guardrails are absent; Bankrbot shows prompts are not controls; Base/MetaMask converge on wallet-enforced caps.

recommendations.recommendation: No capability may be granted by an action the adversary controls: holding or receiving the NFT unlocks viewing and human actions only; an agent's value-moving rights require a holder-signed grantSession to a named key. Encode as a tested invariant.
recommendations.rationale: Bankrbot step 1 escalated privileges by transferring an NFT to the agent's wallet.

recommendations.recommendation: Write ERC-8004-shaped feedback/validation only from settlement paths (escrow release, bond slash, voucher settlement) via a separate permissionless publishFeedback(receiptId) step, tagged escrow-released/bond-slashed/voucher-settled with the rated agent bound separately from payee; never surface getSummary without clientAddresses.
recommendations.rationale: 59-91% Sybil reviewers; maintainers' issue #99; the codebase forbids try/catch around optional side effects on gas-estimated paths, so decouple instead.

recommendations.recommendation: Pin every machine-readable catalog (MCP tool schemas, A2A skills, Desk selector configs) by keccak exposed on chain; bridges refuse to run if the fetched catalog hash differs.
recommendations.rationale: Neutralises MCP tool-definition rug pulls (CVE-2025-54136) structurally; ANIMA's manifestOf already exposes a hash.

recommendations.recommendation: Adopt the ERC-8183 job state machine and events for hiring/escrow, with fund(jobId, expectedBudget) and a non-hookable permissionless claimRefund; expose IACPHook so launchpad/vault can act as hooks.
recommendations.rationale: Composability with Virtuals ACP tooling (18k+ agents) at near-zero design cost; WorkEscrow already has the same lifecycle.

recommendations.recommendation: Serve agent-facing surfaces from chain: /llms.txt and /token/<id>/llms.txt, .md twins, Link rel=alternate/describedby headers, /.well-known/agent-card.json (A2A 1.0 fields) and /.well-known/agent-registration.json; read-only, no JS.
recommendations.rationale: llms.txt v2 allows subpaths and headers; ERC-5219 responses carry headers; zero cost to the human product.

recommendations.recommendation: One gate, two principals: the site's connect-wallet flow accepts SIWE for the holder, SIWA for the token's agent (agentRegistry = our token, verified via the ERC-6551 account's isValidSignature), and session keys only for granted selectors; serve SIWA skill instructions from chain.
recommendations.rationale: Base recommends SIWA; SIWA supports ERC-6551 signers; keyring-proxy pattern keeps keys out of the agent process.

recommendations.recommendation: Publish OASF skills[]/domains[] ids and MCP/A2A version strings in the registration file; generate A2A skills[].inputSchema/outputSchema from the ABI.
recommendations.rationale: ERC-8004 services example and OASF record guide; ANIMA already generates a function index.

recommendations.recommendation: x402: set x402Support only for resources that really settle; emit AgentComms inbox prices and InferenceMeter vouchers as x402 PaymentRequirements (CAIP-2 network, atomic amount, asset, payTo = token account); accept EIP-3009 authorizations where contracts pull ERC-20s.
recommendations.rationale: x402 v2 is vendor-neutral under the Linux Foundation; ERC-8004 feedback already has a proofOfPayment slot.

recommendations.recommendation: Keep ERC-7857 as an adapted design (seal policy, re-key evidence) and do not claim conformance unless verifier(), iTransfer and authorizeUsage are implemented; document the residual-knowledge limit.
recommendations.rationale: ERC-7857 is Final but relies on an out-of-scope Sealed Executor and its ZKP path is TODO; IPSEITY's Standards.sol already argues this.

recommendations.recommendation: Use ERC-7656 linked services with deterministic addresses for swap, messaging, launchpad and vault instead of growing the token.
recommendations.rationale: Keeps every contract under EIP-170 and lets the agent card list counterfactual endpoints.

recommendations.recommendation: Mirror-register in the canonical per-chain ERC-8004 singleton with registrations[] listing both ids, treating it as discovery only.
recommendations.rationale: 8004scan/SIWA defaults may index only canonical addresses; the singleton is upgradeable so it must not be a correctness dependency.

recommendations.recommendation: Support ERC-8001 multi-party intents for agent-to-agent deals needing both sides' acceptances, and ERC-8126 attestations as optional validation-registry signals.
recommendations.rationale: Both are listed Final by secondary surveys (unverified) and compose with ERC-8004.

recommendations.recommendation: Sign the A2A card with the token's account (ERC-1271 over the canonical card) in metadata alongside JWS, and propose it as an A2A extension.
recommendations.rationale: A2A 1.0 signs cards with JWS; an on-chain identity has no JWK but does have an ERC-1271 signer.

recommendations.recommendation: Allow attenuated sub-sessions (child keys with strictly smaller budget/window/allowlist) and commit a workflow hash in submit() deliverables.
recommendations.rationale: Fleet budgeting pattern from agent-wallet practice; PR #1815's agentWorkflowHash idea.

recommendations.recommendation: Do not add admin keys, diamondCut or upgradeable registries; do not load manifest JavaScript or ERC-5169 token scripts; do not rely on prompt-level guardrails, MCP token passthrough, or unsigned shared memory.
recommendations.rationale: Both repos' invariants; ClawHub supply-chain flood; MCP security best practices; ElizaOS memory injection.

recommendations.recommendation: Do not claim ERC-7857 compliance via supportsInterface without a verifier, and do not present unfiltered ERC-8004 getSummary values as reputation.
recommendations.rationale: False conformance invites marketplace green checks; Sybil rates make unfiltered summaries meaningless.

special_ideas: The agent card is minted with the token: tokenURI returns ERC-721 metadata + ERC-8004 registration-v1 + nested A2A AgentCard + MCP-shaped tool catalog, all generated from chain state and hash-pinned.

Settlement-grounded reputation as a product: every feedback record provably cannot exist without an escrow release, bond slash or voucher settlement in the same protocol; publish the tag convention and a verifier (what ERC-8004 issue #99 asks for).
An on-chain llms.txt per token (/token/<id>/llms.txt) with .md twins and Link headers served by Premises; first NFT legible to coding agents and Lighthouse's agentic audit.
One gate, two principals: SIWE for the human holder, SIWA for the token's agent, both verified against the same ERC-6551 account, with the UI showing which principal acts and what its session may do.
Non-escalating capabilities: a test-enforced invariant that receiving any token never changes an agent's authority, making the Bankrbot class impossible by construction.
Rug-pull-proof tools: MCP/A2A catalogs derived from on-chain selectors with a published hash; bridges refuse divergent catalogs.

x402-shaped priced attention: AgentComms inbox prices and inference vouchers emitted as x402 PaymentRequirements so any x402 client can pay the agent without bespoke code; no facilitator needed because settlement is on chain.
ERC-8183-native hiring with launchpad as a BiddingHook and vault as a FundTransferHook, composable with Virtuals ACP tooling.
Counterfactual capabilities: ERC-7656 deterministic addresses let the agent card list swap/vault/launchpad/messaging endpoints before deployment.
A kill-switch as a feature: guardian-may-only-pause plus dispute locks is the human-in-the-loop control Bankr removed; advertise it in supportedTrust and the card.
Validation-registry sink for TEE attestations: declareModel (model id, weight root, runtime measurement) plus ValidationRegistry are already the right shape for ERC-8004's pending TEE revision.
open_questions: ERC-8004's Validation Registry revision (TEE) is promised later in 2026: implement to the current text and version-gate, or wait? Which TEE oracles ship first?
Do 8004scan, SIWA default criteria and Agent0 index arbitrary ERC-8004-shaped registries, or only the canonical singleton addresses? If only canonical, mirror-registration becomes a must.
A2A 1.0 requires JWS for signed cards: will verifiers accept an ERC-1271 extension, and which canonicalisation library behaves identically on chain and off?
What is the minimal honest 'MCP from chain' story (static tool catalog plus holder-run local bridge) and how is the bridge kept from becoming a confused deputy?
Should our contracts accept EIP-3009 authorizations directly (no facilitator), and how does that interact with the money-moves-by-pull ledger rule?
ERC-8128's specification text is unreachable (404 on all canonical hosts on 2026-10-02); confirm its status and header semantics before citing it in our spec.
Which chains carry which agent registrations across our five id bands, and does the agent card list per-chain registrations?
Does an agent-launched token on the launchpad need a regulated-mandate/attestation gate (ERC-8226, unverified)?
Numbers to re-measure before publication: x402 volume, '45,000 agents at launch', Virtuals aGDP, ClawHub counts — all secondary today.
